findings.title: Handle an empty destination calendar array before checking Google Meet
findings.body: When `destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]`, destructuring leaves `mainHostDestinationCalendar` undefined and accessing `.integration` throws. This happens while creating events that use Google Meet but have no destination calendar, so booking creation fails instead of following the previous fallback behavior.

findings.title: Select the destination calendar for the current host credential
findings.body: Collective bookings pass the full destination-calendar array to each host's calendar service, but this always selects element zero. For every secondary Office 365 host, the request then targets the first host's calendar ID using the secondary host's access token. The request fails or creates the event in the wrong calendar, leaving those hosts without the booking. Select the destination associated with the current credential instead.

findings.title: Do not use the first host's calendar for every Lark credential
findings.body: Each collective host's Lark service receives the full destination-calendar array, but this selects only its first entry. A secondary host's credential is therefore used against the first host's calendar ID, which can fail authorization or put the event in the wrong calendar. Select the destination belonging to the current credential.

findings.title: Create CalDAV events in the calendar belonging to the current host
findings.body: For collective bookings, each host's CalDAV service receives the entire destination-calendar array, but this filters calendars using only the first destination. Secondary hosts' credentials consequently try to create the event at the first host's calendar URL; that URL may be inaccessible with their credentials, so their calendar event is not created. Match the destination to the current credential.

findings.title: Use the current host's destination email in the Google attendee list
findings.body: The Google event is inserted into the calendar selected by `credentialId`, but the organizer attendee email is always taken from the first destination calendar. For a secondary host's event, this identifies the first host as the organizer instead of the host whose calendar is being used, so the event can be attributed to or invite the wrong host. Choose the destination matching `credentialId` here too.

findings.title: Fall back to the destination calendar when updating legacy references
findings.body: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, this searches for a destination whose `externalId` is also absent, so it returns `undefined` rather than the configured destination calendar. Updates for bookings with legacy references that lack an external calendar ID are then sent without a valid Google `calendarId` and fail. Fall back to the appropriate destination calendar, as the previous implementation did.

findings.title: Delete legacy Google events from their configured destination calendar
findings.body: If a reference has no `externalCalendarId`, this lookup searches for a destination with an undefined external ID and returns no calendar. The subsequent fallback is `primary`, even when the event was created on a configured non-primary destination calendar. Google returns 404 for that deletion, which this method treats as success, leaving the event orphaned in the calendar.
